title: Teach live acceptance and the demo CLI to authenticate
description:
**Phase 3 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 1ebc7d, fac2ee
- **Runs in parallel with:** 5f0c4c, 5558db, 79578e
- **Unblocks:** 7b4616, which cannot be called done without it

---
**Found by inversion: what breaks quietly and costs a day before anyone sees why?**

Every phase in this plan ends with the instruction to run sh scripts/live_aws_thin_turn.sh development. That script, tests/test_live_aws_thin_turn.py, and the thin-turn demo CLI all speak the current contract: X-Tenant-Id in a header, no credential. The moment 79578e reshapes the routes and 7b4616 flips enforcement, all three fail against every environment, and the failure looks like a broken deploy rather than a stale client.

They are our own tooling, so they authenticate as a worker with a minted credential from fac2ee, not as a person. Do not add a test-only bypass to the front door. That is a second authentication path and the repository does not keep two.

**Done when:** the live script, the pytest live path, and the demo CLI all pass against development with enforcement on, using a real credential.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**This card did exactly what it was written to do, and the commit convention slipped again.**

Finding b3e12c is the whole argument for this card: in-process gates use moto and were green, and only a named deploy against real AWS showed that worker credentials do not survive a Lambda recycle. That is the gap the card exists to close, found on its first exercise.

**Second occurrence of the commit type problem.** `Teach live acceptance and demo CLI org paths and worker bearer auth (#142)` again carries no conventional-commit type, one cycle after the same note on #140. Two of the last four feature merges now contribute no version bump and no changelog entry, and both of them are the security-relevant ones: worker authentication and the path migration that closed the tenant header.

AGENTS.md ties releases from `main` to these messages. At promotion, the range that ships authentication would describe neither piece of it. Worth a habit rather than a reminder each time.
